findings.title: The coordinator has not yet confirmed the FOR KEY SHARE NOWAIT locks on the FK parents (organization, project, acting auth.users row). No race covers the org and user locks, and the user lock adds a new production privilege dependency.
findings.evidence:
Migration :82-90 adds three KEY SHARE NOWAIT locks beyond the rows amendment d0162954 lists. I re-ran mutations on the live function (psql CREATE OR REPLACE after a reset under /tmp/ovd-supabase.lock, then restored):
- Without the project lock: R7 fails with `delete={"error": "deadlock detected", "sqlstate": "40P01"}`, Failed 1/76 (test 70). So the project lock is necessary and proven.
- Without the org and user locks: Result PASS, 76/76. Only the static vitest pins them (xometry-admission-lock-migration.test.ts:49-57).

A new risk the PR body does not mention: FOR KEY SHARE needs UPDATE privilege on the target table. The helper is SECURITY DEFINER and owned by postgres, so it needs UPDATE on auth.users. This is the first migration in the tree that needs that; grep finds no prior UPDATE, INSERT or DELETE on auth.users. Locally, auth.users is owned by supabase_auth_admin, postgres is not superuser, and information_schema shows the image grants postgres INSERT, SELECT, UPDATE, DELETE and more. Hosted and production grant parity is not verified here. If the grant is missing, every fresh dispatch would fail with 42501, which the handler does not map to busy.
findings.suggested_fix: The coordinator decides whether to keep the org and user locks. If the user lock stays, check `has_table_privilege('postgres','auth.users','UPDATE')` on the hosted target before the protected apply. The PR says the org and user locks only close admin and GoTrue waits, so dropping them is another option. Keep the project lock either way: R7 depends on it.

findings.title: The OVD-598 issue description does not state the precise invariant sentence
findings.evidence:
The spec says the migration header, the OVD-598 issue and the PR body must state the claim "after taking its NOWAIT locks the request waits only on the founding-beta shared advisory lock".
- The migration header (:30-34) and the PR body ('Invariant') state it.
- The issue description's amended first criterion only says "so the request never upgrades a lock or waits on a row it later writes".
- The exact claim appears in the coordinator's comment d0162954, not in the description.
findings.suggested_fix: Add the invariant sentence to the amended acceptance criterion in the issue description.

findings.title: The invariant's justification covers only the exclusive holder; lock-queue fairness also brings in the other shared holders (no cycle exists today)
findings.evidence:
Header :33-34 and the PR body say the founding-beta wait is safe because its sole exclusive holder, admin enrollment, touches none of the request's rows. That is incomplete:
- Once an admin enrollment is queued for the exclusive lock, Postgres queues the request's new shared acquisition behind it.
- The admin in turn waits on every current shared holder, so the request can transitively wait on those holders.

I checked every function that takes `founding-beta:<org>` shared. None of them takes the request's rows after that lock:
- api_authorize_xometry_beta_worker_dispatch and api_authorize_provider_worker_dispatch take their row locks before the shared lock.
- api_get_quote_access only reads.
- The generic resolver locks its own job first.
- Same-job paths are serialized by quote-lane-submit, and same-org legacy requests by free-quote-subject:organization.

So no cycle exists today. The written argument should name this condition so that future shared holders are checked against it.
findings.suggested_fix: Add one sentence: every holder of the founding-beta shared lock takes its row locks before that lock and never waits afterwards on a row this request holds.

findings.title: Phantom rows are not covered by the pre-lock set (theoretical)
findings.evidence:
Inserts take FOR KEY SHARE on their FK parents. That is compatible with the request's FNKU on the job and FOR SHARE on parts, so a part can be inserted into the job after the helper runs.
- If it commits before the resolver reads, the resolver's exactly-one-part check catches it (`xometry_beta_exactly_one_part_required`).
- If it commits between the resolver and the impl's eligibility read, the impl's vendor_quote_results and lane FK checks could take KEY SHARE on an unlocked part.

The PR body already lists the part count as an unlocked residual. Separately, private.request_automatic_quote_impl also inserts this line item, but it has no callers and only its owner can execute it, so the write-target table's list of line-item inserters is complete for reachable code.
findings.suggested_fix: No code change needed. Optionally add one line to the residual list.
